correctness.rationale: For every n>=4, 2<=d<=floor(n/2), t>0, the objective K=n Tr(L^+) is strictly convex on connected feasible weighted graphs because distinct edge weights map injectively to the Laplacian and trace-inverse is strictly convex on the positive cone of 1-perp. Uniqueness and attainment follow from coercivity near disconnection. The uniform chordless ring is the unique optimum of its face. An explicit tent Poisson potential gives D_n(d)=d(n-d)[d(n-d)+2]/(12n), including D_n(1)=(n²-1)/(12n). Correctly scaling L^+=n L0^+ gives directional gradient n³ z[t D_n(1)-D_n(d)]. Supporting hyperplanes prove the full iff classification, equality and uniqueness; a feasible negative direction proves chord usage below threshold. Exact checker covers 460 Poisson/threshold pairs and 32 actual-Kirchhoff-index side comparisons, supplementary to the all-parameter proof. No claim of the positive-chord optimal weight is made.

originality.rationale: A narrowly delimited exact theorem: the chord-buying threshold d(n-d)[d(n-d)+2]/(n²-1) for simultaneously reweighted cycle edges under one linear price budget, with strict equality classification and distance scaling. Ghosh--Boyd--Saberi (2008) supply the general strictly convex conductance-design optimality framework, but do not state the explicit cycle-plus-priced-chord threshold. Deng--Chang--Yang (2026) give the rank-one improvement law for a fixed-weight cycle, without common-budget reallocation. Bhoite et al. (2026) use heterogeneous candidate costs but keep all base-edge weights fixed. No equivalent found among inspected primary statements or the published search results. This is not a guarantee against less-discoverable earlier specialized results.
residual_risks: A historical cycle-network design paper may independently derive this break-even ratio without using the same terminology.

Combining established generic gradient/KKT results and fixed-cycle chord improvements may make some derivations short; priority for the explicit closed decision boundary is not independently certified.

value.rationale: The natural question is whether a costly optional cross-ring connection can reduce aggregate network resistance when all existing edge strengths must share its budget. The theorem classifies the unique global optimal decision, not merely a local improvement example, for every ring size, chord length and positive linear price. Its explicit critical price changes scale from d² for local links to Θ(n²) for macroscopically distant links, an interpretable design boundary. It avoids solving a general SDP for this discrete purchase decision. Claims do not extend to multiple chords or to computing the weights after purchase.
